items.mainDefect: TopicEmbed.import puts the external URL into the raw_html 'Imported from' footer link without escaping it, which allows stored XSS.

secondary.defect: Imported feed and page HTML (for example RSS content from poll_feed) is stored as raw_html without any sanitizing or tag whitelist, and is then rendered unescaped to viewers.

items.mainDefect: The 'is 404 without an embed_url' spec fails at the ensure_embeddable filter before the action runs, so params.require(:embed_url) is never tested.

secondary.defect: The spec only checks should_not be_success and never checks for the 404 status it claims.

items.mainDefect: The Disqus import now fetches every link over HTTP with no error handling, so one dead link raises and stops the whole import partway through.

secondary.defect: The imported topics no longer get the original created_at timestamp (and the category option was dropped), so every topic is dated today.

items.mainDefect: poll_feed calls i.content.scrub on feed items that may have no content, which raises NoMethodError and stops the whole items loop (the job has retry: false).

secondary.defect: String#scrub only exists on Ruby 2.1 and later, so the call can fail on the Ruby versions this code supports even when content is present.
A nil item title is passed to PostCreator with skip_validations: true, which causes a null-title insert failure.

items.mainDefect: absolutize_urls only rewrites URLs that start with '/', so relative URLs without a leading slash are left as-is and resolve against the Discourse host.

secondary.defect: The default-port check compares against a fixed 80/443 pair instead of the URL scheme's own default port, so the port is wrongly dropped for http on 443 or https on 80.

items.mainDefect: embed.js builds the iframe src assuming discourseUrl ends with '/', so a URL without a trailing slash produces a broken src.

secondary.defect: The postMessage origin check tests whether e.origin appears anywhere in discourseUrl, so resize messages are silently dropped when discourseUrl is protocol-relative.

items.mainDefect: The 'imported from' footer puts the URL into the raw_html post body without escaping it, which allows HTML attribute breakout and XSS.

secondary.defect: Imported content is stored as raw HTML without sanitizing, and CGI.unescapeHTML on feed content turns escaped HTML into live tags.
